calls.prompt:
Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

Affected areas and owners:
- pharmacy-ops: Dispensing, controlled substances (DEA), pharmacist scope, vaccines → Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations)
- drug-safety: OTC products, labeling, recalls, shortages (FDA) → Daniel Brooks (Drug Safety & Quality)
- payers: Medicare Part D, Medicaid and insurer billing (CMS) → Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement)
- privacy-people: Patient privacy (HIPAA), records, store workforce → Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-13, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-13; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

I found four documents in the 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 window that affect CornerCare. My searches were not an exhaustive scan of that week's issues, so other documents may exist. I confirmed one deadline and no effective dates beyond the first item.

**1. DEA interim final rule placing oveporexton (Orzeyful) in Schedule IV**
- **Document number:** 2026-23075
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23075/schedules-of-controlled-substances-placement-of-oveporexton-in-schedule-iv
- **Key deadline:** The rule is effective November 12, 2026. Comments are due by December 14, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a rule that took effect within the 30 days before 11-13, and its comment deadline is under 90 days away.
- **Owner:** pharmacy-ops (Priya Raman)
- **Reason:** FDA approved the drug for narcolepsy type 1 in adults on August 5, 2026. It is now a Schedule IV controlled substance, so CornerCare's dispensing, inventory, recordkeeping and prescription rules apply to it.
- **Action:** Add oveporexton to the controlled-substance dispensing, inventory and recordkeeping workflows now, and decide whether to comment by December 14.

**2. CMS final rule: Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Part D**
- **Document number:** 2026-22792 (CMS-4215-F)
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22792/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program-and-medicare-prescription-drug-benefit-program
- **Key deadline:** I did not find an effective or compliance date in the search results. Confirm it in the full text.
- **Tier:** High. It is a final rule, but I could not confirm that it took effect in the last 30 days. If its effective date falls before 2027-02-11, treat it as Critical.
- **Owner:** payers (Lucia Moreno)
- **Reason:** The rule finalizes and codifies the Negotiation Program and sets new Part D policies. The negotiated price is the price paid to the network pharmacy for a covered Part D drug dispensed to a plan enrollee, so it affects pharmacy payment and claims.
- **Action:** Review the Part D pharmacy payment and claims provisions for selected drugs, and check that billing and reimbursement processes will meet them.

**3. DEA proposed 2027 aggregate production quotas** (borderline: it is aimed at manufacturers)
- **Document number:** 2026-22843
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22843/proposed-aggregate-production-quotas-for-schedule-i-and-ii-controlled-substances-and-assessment-of
- **Key deadline:** The comment deadline was not in the retrieved text. Check the document.
- **Tier:** Medium. It is a notice with a comment period.
- **Owner:** drug-safety (Daniel Brooks)
- **Reason:** DEA proposes higher 2027 quotas for the stimulants d,l-amphetamine and d-amphetamine, which is relevant to ADHD medicine supply on CornerCare's shelves.
- **Action:** Track the quota levels for ADHD stimulants and opioids as an input to shortage planning. Comment only if supply is a concern.

**4. DEA adjustment to the 2026 aggregate production quotas** (borderline: it is aimed at manufacturers)
- **Document number:** 2026-22842
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22842/adjustment-to-the-2026-aggregate-production-quota-for-dl-amphetamine-d-amphetamine-for-sale
- **Key deadline:** None confirmed.
- **Tier:** Low. I found no confirmed comment deadline.
- **Owner:** drug-safety (Daniel Brooks)
- **Reason:** DEA is adjusting the 2026 quotas for d,l-amphetamine, d-amphetamine (for sale), hydromorphone and methylphenidate (for sale). DEA found multiple manufacturers reporting a domestic shortage of methylphenidate tablets and film.
- **Action:** Pass the information to purchasing and shortage-monitoring staff. No compliance step is required.

**Items I looked at and left out**
- The HIPAA Privacy Rule final rule (2026-23429) was published November 19, outside the window.
- The CMS "Cutting Administrative Requirements" proposed rule (2026-22812) targets hospitals and nursing homes.
- The CMS paperwork notices from November 12–13, the FDA real-world-evidence request for information and the DOL unemployment work-search proposed rule do not apply to a retail pharmacy.
- The DEA decisions and orders about individual practitioners do not apply either.
